newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds becalmed in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds becalmed in thin market.

text.p: Irish government bonds were slightly weaker in a thin market caused by the closure of the UK due to a bank holiday and a directionless Europe, dealers said.
"It's very, very quiet and we are not getting much guidance from international markets because they are quiet too in the absence of the UK," one dealer said.
"Ten to fifteen pence would just about sum up the difference over last week's levels," the dealer added.
Dealers said last week's unexpected repo rate cut by the Bundesbank remained the focus of activity, however subdued, and the effects were still working their way through the market.
"Last week's steepening of the curve is still the focus. It has tigthened us by one or two points," another dealer said.
By 1440 GMT the the 8.00 percent bond due 2000 was at 103.87. to yield 6.76 percent versus 103.95 and a yield of 6.74 percent at Friday's close.
The 8.00 percent bond due 2006 was seen at 102.87 to yield 7.43 per cent against a Friday close of 103.05.
